newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends 6.1 centavos off, big dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends 6.1 centavos off, big dlr demand.

text.p: The Mexican peso MXAAA closed considerably weaker on Friday after a speculative and nervous session, in which the dollar was in heavy demand by foreign investors, traders said.
"Foreign investors stepped in with many orders to buy (dollars) as soon as the peso hit 7.66 per dollar, that caused the peso to snowball," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 6.1 and 6.9 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.6750/7.6800 and 7.6700/7.6750 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed 1.9 centavos off at 7.6000/7.6030 per dollar.
Traders said that the late slump in the stock market was a sign of foreigners buying dollars in large amounts. The blue chip IPC index was 15.95 points off, or 0.47 percent, at 3,349.40.
"The bolsa began to fall when foreign investors took fright at the weakening peso and stepped out of stocks," a trader said. "This in turn weakened the peso when they bought dollars."

Dollars were in heavier demand from foreign investors who wished to cover positions ahead of Monday, when U.S. banks will be closed. Also, U.S. consumer prices due to be announced on Wednesday have put investors on alert, traders said.

Other traders pointed out that the peso may also have slid due to mounting pressure in recent weeks from talk that the peso has stood still against the dollar for almost a year, and export companies are thus losing their competitive edge.
"It was like a pressure cooker...it's better that we have a gradual slide between now and December than a sudden last-minute jolt," said one peso trader.
Other traders pointed out that the weak peso could lead to hikes in primary rates next week to prevent the currency weakening too quickly.
"The peso was too strong, but it's also important to avoid speculation getting out of hand," said another trader.
Traders felt that the peso could undergo a respite on Monday when U.S. banks will be closed.
